steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: When you look up from this angle, you can see the sky through the narrow gap between the high walls of the alley. Despite its small size, the sky appears incredibly blue and vast.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I don't normally have the chance or desire to gaze upon the sky like this, but today, I realize it's quite nice.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: The only thing that makes this feel less comfortable is the rock against my upper back. But that's okay, I've grown numb to the pain.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: A flock of white birds fly across that tiny gap, free and unrestrained. In the meantime, my life is slowly draining away.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I always knew this would happen eventually, one way or another. After all, tomorrow is not guaranteed in this line of work; my life could end anytime and anywhere, nothing surprising.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: My vision starts to blur, a sign of hallucinations due to extreme weakness.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I hear jumbled footsteps that appear close one moment, and distant the next.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Out of nowhere, I think of the goldfish in the corner of the living room, their blood-red tails swaying in the water before my eyes.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Some say that before death, one sees what they can't let go of, and the person they want to see the most.
...Angell? Angell!

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Seems like it's true.
What happened?! Stay with me...

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Because just before I fall into complete darkness, I see your face.
In a corner of the MBCC cafeteria, you sit opposite Angell at a rather inconspicuous dining table.
Between you are a few empty plates that were filled with side dishes, along with a stack of bowls.
Since it's not mealtime, there aren't many people in the cafeteria, but Angell still receives some curious gaze from the people who pass by.
However, she remains calm and composed, like she usually does, and finishes her sixth bowl of red bean soup, unfazed by the unfamiliar surroundings.
Finding Angell unconscious in a Syndicate alley nearly sent you into a panic. You hastily rush her back to the MBCC for urgent medical care.
Fortunately, the physical examination showed that she simply passed out from extreme hunger, and she was fine after some glucose.
When was the last time you ate...?
Angell eats quietly, even elegantly, but her speed is astonishing. As her bowl empties once more, you push your untouched bowl of red bean soup towards her.
She accepts without hesitation, simply nodding her thanks.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Can't remember, but it's been quite a while.
Angell brushes off the question, clearly unwilling to dwell on this topic.
Okay...
After she devours another bowl of soup, you offer:
Do you want more? If it's still not enough, I can cook some more...

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Thanks, but it's okay.
She sets down her spoon and the empty bowl.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I'm full now.
She looks at you, then at the empty bowl in front of her, and smiles with a hint of nostalgia.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Your red bean soup tastes amazing, just like always. I never thought I'd have it again.
She smiles at you across the table, reminding you of the time back at the safe house. You smile back at her.
Nonsense. I'm right here. You can always tell me when you have a craving.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: ...Thank you.
After expressing her gratitude once more, Angell gets up, ready to leave, but you hold her back.
Angell, wait.
I know you're more than capable of getting out of the Bureau whenever you want, but would you mind if we talk a bit more elsewhere? It's just the standard procedure around here.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: What procedure?
Despite not knowing what you mean by "procedure," Angell follows you, heading deeper into the Bureau.
Angell takes a seat in the interrogation room, scanning the shackles hanging from the armrests, various security devices in the room, and the video camera in the corner that's been turned off.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Is this where you usually interrogate Sinners?
She sounds indifferent, showing no emotion, but you can't help feeling nervous. Worried she might misunderstand, you hurriedly explain.
Don't worry. There are no guards outside, and I didn't put the shackles on you. This is just the standard procedure for all new Sinners.
Just think of it as us finding a quieter place to talk, okay?
Angell's gaze softens as she looks back at you.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I'm alright, but you seem really nervous.
Angell leaves you speechless for a moment, then the corner of her lips curls up. Seemingly in a good mood, she initiates a new topic of conversation.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: You want to talk, let's talk.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Let's start with... how did you find me?
You didn't just stumble upon her, of course.
After sending you back, Angell vanished completely like a raindrop fallen into the deep waters of the dark web.

It's difficult for ordinary people and the authorities to reach the deeper ends of the dark web. You found nothing despite using every possible means and searching through every channel you could think of.

But yesterday, you saw a post about "Angell's whereabouts" on the surface of the dark web. You took your chances and bought the information from them, and that's how you found Angell, who had passed out on the street.
Someone was selling your intel on the dark web yesterday. Is it because you made too many enemies in the kidnapping mission, and they wanted revenge?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: ...It could be.
Angell doesn't seem too surprised, merely nodding thoughtfully.
She doesn't question who provided the information, but you couldn't tell her even if she did. The poster used a disposable account, and you couldn't find any useful information from it.
Speaking of which...

options: Could you help me with something?

choices.text: Could you help me with something?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: What?
You open a file and push it across the table to Angell.
test
test
test
test
test
test
This is the operation report for the entire case.
I couldn't see many things clearly when they were happening, but I'm beginning to piece them together while reviewing the case and writing the report.
There are still some details I'm not too sure about. Could you help verify them?
Angell glances at the report and says without hesitation:

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Yes, I can.
Alright, let's start with the background of this case.
With the reconstruction of the West District underway, the gangs found it increasingly difficult to survive, forcing them to flee to this mysterious dark web created by some unknown figure.
The dark web's covert and intricate nature allows them to carry out a series of attacks on key figures in the West District, including me, making it difficult for the authorities to respond quickly.
Angell narrows her eyes, holding back what she wants to say and letting you continue.
This was our analysis at first, but as the operation unfolded, we realized we had overlooked a very important force—
The masterminds hidden in the deeper area of the dark web.
Angell nods slightly in agreement.

As you said before, people like us only have access to the surface of the dark web. So, at first, I assumed that the first round of the counterattacks I secretly organized using your account had eliminated all the enemies.

But then you told me about the deeper area of the dark web, and the results of the operation showed that there indeed was a hidden force—the real gang leaders and the Hypercube company who are upset by the new mines.
They were the real masterminds and financiers. The people we caught before were just thugs and minions.
We didn't realize they were behind the scenes and almost let them slip away. If it weren't for your covert assistance, we would never been able to solve the case.
Angell's gaze flickers.
You flip through the report and point to the "Joint Operation" section.
You put news about me on the dark web, asking those who were interested to come find you with their offers. But selling me for a good price wasn't your real intention, was it?
Since there's nothing to hide anymore, Angell admits openly.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: No. I leaked your information to bait them.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Those people were so eager to get rid of you and the news threw them off. They were worried you'd be rescued, so they hastily recruited some people to make a second assassination attempt.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: They were ill-prepared. That's why they gave themselves away, and finally gave you the chance to solve the case.
You nod with a smile.
And that's not the only time you've helped me.
Angell looks at you, surprised and puzzled.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: What do you mean?

I'm talking about the time you went out every night and came back injured. You never told me what you were up to, but come to think of it, you must have been dealing with those who wanted to kill me, right?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: ...Yes.
For protecting me all this time.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: No need.
Angell shakes her head, but her gaze softens.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I was just doing what the client wanted. The instructions were very clear: kidnap and guard the MBCC Chief until delivery, no killing involved.
You ponder for a moment, a new doubt crossing your mind.
Was that job from a gang?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Yes.
Isn't that strange? Those people clearly wanted me dead.
...Perhaps the job was tampered with?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: It's possible.

A dark web case is inherently far more challenging to tackle than typical cases, and this time we even found out about the dark web's deeper layer. What exactly is this dark web? What encryption technology does it use? When was it developed, and by whom?
Angell goes deep into thought for a moment.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I only know that the technology used by the dark web is extremely bizarre and highly secure, making it difficult to crack... I know nothing about its origins and creators.
Then, who do you think has the ability to interfere with the jobs in the deep dark web?
After a brief silence, Angell lowers her gaze.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: No idea. I'm just a contractor who only cares about completing the jobs.
I see.
Angell moves in her seat to adjust her posture, and you catch a glimpse of a few wounds under the hem of her clothes that weren't there before.
I've got everything I need. Now, let's talk about you.
What happened to you? How come you passed out on the streets?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I had no money, couldn't afford to eat.
Such a candid and straightforward answer leaves you momentarily speechless.
This is not an easy thing to admit openly, but Angell shows no sign of embarrassment.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: This job has caused me a great deal of trouble. Though you might have caught all the gangsters, many others took this opportunity to seek revenge. Many of them were also hitmen.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: They thought I had betrayed the dark web and turned to the authorities. I know a lot of their secrets, so those guys are trying to get rid of me.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I've been followed closely by them 24/7. I couldn't withdraw money, or go back to the safe house to get food...

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: That's why I ended up like that.
Despite her light and matter-of-fact tone, you can imagine the hardship she went through.
...Did that job affect your credibility on the dark web?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Not really. No one cares about credibility there. After I deal with those guys, business will only get better, because I've proven myself.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Besides, it's not like I betrayed my client. I did exactly what the job asked me to do. They wanted me to protect you by kidnapping you, they will thank me for it.
Good.
The conversation winds down. Angell stares at you for a bit.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Anyway, thanks for searching for me and the meal. Once everything is settled, I will repay you.
You understand the meaning behind her words—she doesn't plan to stay at the MBCC.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: What do you mean?
Well, you've got nowhere else to go right now, why not stay here for a couple more days?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: ...Is this how you want me to repay you?
Yeah. I happen to be on a break at the moment, so you could join me for a bit of a holiday.

When you were living together, you had been trying to show her the beauty of the sunlit world by picking certain jobs for her, but you also wanted to take her out on the streets to experience the life of ordinary people.
This is something you've always wanted to do since you first met her, but you never had the chance. And now, this might be the perfect opportunity.
She always says she's meant to lurk in the shadows, but once she feels the sun's warmth and witnesses the flourishing lives under the sunlight, perhaps she will change her mind.
She frowns, likely sensing your intention.
However, perhaps due to your help this time, or because she's gotten used to you planning things for her, she cannot bring herself to refuse.
Noticing her silence, you give a sly smile.
Alright, since you're not saying anything, I'll assume you agree.
I'll plan our trip for the next couple of days.
